title: The Year of Mercy (2015–2016)
hookLine: a jubilee where Doors of Mercy opened in cathedrals around the world, not only in Rome
last: A POOR CHURCH FOR THE POOR.

lines: A PILGRIMAGE IN A FEW STEPS.
cards: A heavy door, usually sealed shut, swings open, and people walk through it slowly: some touching the frame, some carrying children, some in wheelchairs pushed by friends. It's only a doorway.
On the other side is the same church floor. But in a jubilee year, walking through a Holy Door is a pilgrimage in a few steps.
The best-known Holy Doors are in Rome's great basilicas, and to walk through one of those you had to get there.
Then Pope Francis called a jubilee and asked that doors like this be opened in cathedrals and shrines everywhere, so people who could never travel to Rome could walk through one at home.

teach.b: The year rested on four things. First, the opening line. Francis announced the jubilee in a document named for its first words, Misericordiae vultus, the face of mercy.
It begins by saying that Jesus Christ is the face of the Father's mercy.
Second, the motto: merciful like the Father. It comes from Luke, in the Douay-Rheims: "Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful."
Third, the door. Jesus says in John's Gospel, "I am the door. By me, if any man enter in, he shall be saved." The Holy Door is that line made into wood and hinges.
The document asked that a Door of Mercy be opened in the cathedral of each diocese, and allowed others at churches and shrines.
Walking through it, with confession and prayer, was a way of receiving the jubilee's grace, the indulgence. Fourth, the works.

The document asked Catholics to rediscover the works of mercy. The corporal ones: feed the hungry, give drink to the thirsty, clothe the naked, welcome the stranger, heal the sick, visit the imprisoned, bury the dead.
And the spiritual ones, among them: counsel the doubtful, comfort the afflicted, forgive offenses, bear wrongs patiently, pray for the living and the dead.
Francis also sent out priests he called Missionaries of Mercy, to preach and hear confessions. The door was the symbol; the works were the point.

how: In a jubilee year Catholics make pilgrimage through a Holy Door, usually with confession, Communion and prayer for the pope's intentions; the works of mercy are taught in parishes and practiced through parish outreach.

games.q: you're pope, calling a jubilee of mercy. not every Catholic can travel to Rome. what do you do?
o: tell them to watch it on television.
ask for Doors of Mercy to be opened in cathedrals and shrines everywhere.
hold it only for those who can come.
games.why: Francis asked for a Door of Mercy in each diocese, so the pilgrimage could happen close to home.

practice: Picture the door of a church near you, its handle, its weight, the step up or down, or any doorway you pass through every day.

Choose one work of mercy from the list, the one you'd most like to have done for you, and imagine carrying it through that door. If you pray, say the line from John, I am the door; if not, let the doorway mean something today.

wordCard.voice: Misericordiae vultus. The face of mercy, the document in which Pope Francis announced the Year of Mercy and asked that Holy Doors be opened in cathedrals everywhere.

orig.note: Latin: the face of mercy, the first words and the name of the document announcing the jubilee.
